# An aligned native stack can merge without rebasing onto a newer trunk.

[!git:2.40.0] skip # native stack merges require merge-tree --merge-base

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-10-26T00:03:25Z'

cd repo
git init
git config spice.experiment.merge true
git config spice.forge.shamhub.stacks on
git commit --allow-empty -m 'Initial commit'

shamhub-setup
shamhub new origin alice/example.git
shamhub register alice
git push origin main
env SHAMHUB_USERNAME=alice
gs auth login

git add bottom.txt
gs bc bottom -m 'Add bottom'
git add middle.txt
gs bc middle -m 'Add middle'
git add top.txt
gs bc top -m 'Add top'
gs downstack submit --fill

# Trunk advances independently; the members still align with each other.
gs branch checkout main
git add trunk.txt
git commit -m 'Advance trunk'
git push origin main
git tag before-merge
gs branch checkout top

gs downstack merge --no-prompt
stderr 'All 3 change.s. merged.'
! stderr 'restacked'
! stderr 'Updated #'

# One atomic merge preserves both trunk's new work and the stack's work.
git rev-list --first-parent --count before-merge..main
stdout '^1$'
git log -1 --format=%s main
stdout '^Merge changes #1 through #3$'
git show main:trunk.txt
stdout '^trunk$'
git show main:bottom.txt
stdout '^bottom$'
git show main:middle.txt
stdout '^middle$'
git show main:top.txt
stdout '^top$'

-- repo/bottom.txt --
bottom
-- repo/middle.txt --
middle
-- repo/top.txt --
top
-- repo/trunk.txt --
trunk
